svg.text: Tabernacle of Praise / Four developed directions
DRAFT — NOT FOR PUBLICATION / No logo, typeface, or palette selected
S1 / Responsive Cover
Joined textile folds make a dwelling whose own lifted edges express
response and praise.
OPEN QUESTION: The white opening may suggest a robed figure or flame; the draped silhouette
can suggest a tent venue or sails. Fine fold tips soften at micro sizes, and praise is less
explicit than dwelling.
S2 / Common Ground
Unequal broad surfaces depend on one another to make a single generous
room; gathering creates the dwelling.
OPEN QUESTION: May read as an architectural/cultural institution rather than a church. The
fine left crease closes small; do not assign doctrinal meaning to the number of surfaces.
S3 / Cadenced Wall
A folded wall changes height and turns around a shared forecourt; the
structure itself carries an expressive cadence.
OPEN QUESTION: Could suggest a cultural venue, performance hall, or skyline. Rhythm is a
creative association with praise; architecture alone cannot establish worship.
S4 / Shared Line
The first T becomes the common structure holding the full name together.
OPEN QUESTION: The long overhead line may read as a signboard or roof. The compact T has
weaker distinctiveness without the full name. The single-line arrangement is very wide;
minimum sizes and final clear space are not established.
